correctness.rationale: For all q≥3 and 3≤m<n, rank-q FO³ distinguishes m<n if and only if m<2^(q-1), using the recursively defined F_{q-2,s}(x,y) interval tests. The interval splitting lemma K_r=2K_{r-1}+1 gives a q-round winning Duplicator strategy for any m,n≥2^(q-1), including all repeated choices and moves before the second distinct point appears. This proves full FO indistinguishability, not merely bounded-variable equivalence. For q≤2 the ternary relation cannot be tested on three distinct bound elements; for unrestricted FO² all atomic cyclic-order tests contain repeated variables and are false. The two independent finite checks replayed exactly: three-pebble rank colours for n=3..40 and q=0..6, and interval formula/splitting checks. Finite checks corroborate but do not prove the infinite assertion.

value.rationale: This determines every finite rank-q sentence-equivalence class of a natural relational representation of circular order, and identifies an exact exponential cutoff, sharp minimal representative sizes, and the least distinguishing rank. More substantively, the rank-preserving expressive equivalence of FO³ and full first-order logic on this family contrasts with unrestricted-depth FO² blindness. The two-arc splitting invariant is a structural mechanism rather than an arbitrary numerical observation. It gives a benchmark for resource-bounded finite model theory and demonstrates a precise boundary between variable width and quantifier depth.
